output.brief: The gap looks mostly like a time-in-level effect, not a location effect. Only 32% of remote staff had the 18 months in level the policy requires, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, promotion rates are nearly the same: 20.0% remote and 21.1% office. Nomination and approval rates are also similar. The remaining 1.1-point difference rests on 110 people and could be chance. Don't confirm proximity bias, and don't adopt the three-day office rule. The rule would penalise about 180 people hired on home-based contracts and wouldn't address the real cause. I'm fairly confident (about 80%) in this conclusion. Next steps: hold the proposal and change the dashboard to compare only eligible employees. Re-check that at the FY2027 cycle, when more remote staff will reach eligibility. Also look into why remote staff have shorter tenure: recent remote hiring, or higher exits. I haven't checked that. Manager comments suggest urgent work goes to nearby staff, so track who gets stretch assignments before changing how that work is assigned. Consider clearer communication of promotion criteria to remote staff, since fewer of them say they understand the criteria.
